commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Ricursive Ripple-65B support
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Native support for Ricursive's [Ripple-65B Preview](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview) (`RicursiveForCausalLM`, BF16 and ModelOpt [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4)), its reasoning and tool-call format, and its [DFlash2 draft](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2). Before this PR the only serving path was the authors' out-of-tree SGLang plugin. No open vLLM PR or issue covers this model.

## Claims

- `RicursiveForCausalLM` runs natively with TP, PP, torch.compile and CUDA graphs, without `--trust-remote-code` (built-in `RicursiveConfig`).
- `--reasoning-parser ripple` / `--tool-call-parser ripple`: optional `<think>` plus Hermes-style JSON tool calls. Streaming matches non-streaming output.
- DFlash drafts can declare NoPE layers through `no_rope_layers`. On the Ripple draft this raises mean acceptance length on GSM8K from 4.98 to 7.34.
- Adds a `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview` recipe (NVFP4 default on one B300, BF16 variant, parsers, opt-in DFlash2). It passes `validate-source.mjs` from vllm-project/recipes.
- Adds the missing ZAYA1 trace builder, without which `tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py` and `test_delegating_replay.py` fail at collection on main.

## Validation

All runs on B300.

**Parity against the authors' HF modeling code**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tiny random 10-layer checkpoint (every feature on, 16-token window), eager / compile / TP=2 / PP=2 | mean \|Δlogprob\| 0.009–0.014, equal to the HF bf16-vs-fp32 floor (0.013–0.015) |
| Ripple-65B BF16, 3 prompts of ~2.2K tokens (2× the sliding window), teacher-forced plus 48 greedy tokens | mean \|Δlogprob\| 0.0105, top-1 agreement 99.5%, greedy 48/48 on all three |

**Accuracy** (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, NVFP4 at TP=1)

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Completions, 5-shot | 0.916 | 0.000 |
| Completions, 5-shot, with DFlash2 draft | 0.916 | 0.000 |
| Chat completions, `--reasoning-parser ripple` (content only scored), max 8192 tokens | 0.971 | 0.005 (all 5 hit max tokens while still reasoning) |

**DFlash2 per-position acceptance** (GSM8K 5-shot, `num_speculative_tokens=15`)

| | Mean acceptance length | p1 | p2 | p3 | p4 | p5 | p6 | p8 | p10 | p12 | p15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft NoPE layer rotated (main) | 4.98 | .86 | .71 | .58 | .47 | .39 | .31 | .15 | .07 | .03 | .01 |
| `no_rope_layers` honored (this PR) | 7.34 | .91 | .82 | .73 | .65 | .58 | .52 | .38 | .26 | .17 | .09 |

**Tests**

- `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Ricursive`, `tests/models/test_registry.py -k Ricursive`: pass.
- `tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning` (CPU): 9771 passed.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py test_dflash_causality.py test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/models/test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`: 160 passed.
- New: `tests/parser/engine/test_ripple.py` and the Ripple trace-builder samples; `test_ripple_draft_skips_context_rope_on_nope_layers` in `test_dflash2.py` (draft routing, and NoPE layers keep unrotated context keys).

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000

vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser ripple --reasoning-parser ripple \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 8192 --temperature 0
```
</details>

## Details

- **Model.** Dense 80 layers. Repeating pattern of 4 sliding-window (1024, RoPE) layers and 1 full-attention NoPE layer; PeriNorm (Gemma 3 style pre/post norms); per-head Q/K RMSNorm; fp32 sigmoid output gate; value residuals (`v_proj(lerp(x0, h, sigmoid(λ)))` with `x0` the scaled embeddings); clamped SwiGLU via the existing `SiluAndMulWithClamp`. Q/K/G share one `MergedColumnParallelLinear`; V stays separate because it reads the value-residual blend. The value-residual source is cloned, because the fused add+RMSNorm updates the layer-0 residual in place and would otherwise overwrite it. It travels through PP intermediate tensors, and the model exposes EAGLE-3 aux hidden states for the draft.
- **Parser.** A declarative `ParserEngine` grammar starting in CONTENT. The template's framing newlines (`<think>\n…\n</think>\n`, `\n<tool_call>\n…\n</tool_call>`) are folded into the marker spellings, so they reach neither reasoning nor content. Reasoning is optional, so structured outputs apply from the first token and constrained requests answer directly; this matches the authors' SGLang parser. The markers are multi-token plain text, so the parser is skipped in the single-token replay harness, as PLaMo3 already is.
- **DFlash NoPE.** Ripple's drafter lives in its own subclass (`ricursive_dflash2.py`): a `DFlash2DraftModel` draft that declares `no_rope_layers` is routed to `DFlash2RicursiveDraftModel` in `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`. Its NoPE layers skip the query rotation and restore their unrotated context keys after the shared fused RoPE call. The only shared-code change is moving that fused call into an overridable `DFlashQwen3Model._apply_context_rope`, with no behavior change for other drafts.
- **Reasoning-only streaming.** Without a tool parser (no `--enable-auto-tool-choice`), `parse_delta` passed deltas through raw once the prompt closed reasoning. Ripple's grammar starts in content, so that is always the case. An engine whose grammar can open reasoning from content now parses the whole stream, matching the non-streaming path (`abstract_parser.py`, `adapters.py`). The full `tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning` suite still passes (9771).
- **CI coverage.** The full-size checkpoints are too large for CI, so the parity and GSM8K numbers above were measured locally. `test_ripple.py` joins the other `tests/parser` files on the tethering allowlist while that CI job is disabled.
- **Limitations.** Not tested: ROCm, LoRA, the BF16 checkpoint at TP>1.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and run the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Skip unavailable models before spawning a test process
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In `tests/models/test_initialization.py` and `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py`, mark cases whose model is not available online or needs another transformers version as skipped at collection, so they no longer start a fresh test process only to skip.

## Claims

- These modules run every case in a new interpreter (`create_new_process_for_each_test`, spawn on ROCm). The availability checks ran inside it, so each such case paid 9-11 s to start and then skipped. Now they are skipped before any process starts.
- No skip is added or removed, the skip reasons are unchanged, and the collected test IDs are identical.
- Expected CI saving, from the vllm/ci build 99098 logs and the last 7 days' run rate of main plus PR builds: 64 such cases per build in (MI355 DPX) Basic Models (Extra Initialization) and 19 in (MI355 DPX) Multimodal Processor, about 23 machine-hours a day.

## Validation

Environment: CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a19b0e-d62f-4889-8556-b5c2d4478cbf` (vllm/ci build 99098) with this PR applied as a patch, one MI300X. One run per row (n=1) on a shared machine.

Commands run:

```bash
pytest --collect-only -q models/test_initialization.py models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py   # before and after
pytest -v -s -rs --durations=0 models/test_initialization.py -k "test_can_initialize_large_subset and (Rnj1ForCausalLM or DeepseekV32MTPModel or MiniCPMV4_7ForConditionalGeneration or K2HorizonForCausalLM or MolmoForCausalLM or PhiForCausalLM)"
pytest -v -s -rs --durations=0 models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k "MiniMax-M3 or Molmo-7B-O-0924 or MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize or Qwen2-VL-2B"
pre-commit run --files tests/models/utils.py tests/models/test_initialization.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py
```

| Check | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Collected test IDs (both modules) | 597 | the same 597 |
| init: 4 not available online + 1 transformers version | `call` 9.6-10.6 s each, skipped | skipped at collection, no `call` |
| tensor schema: 2 not available online + 1 transformers version | `call` 9.1 s each, skipped | skipped at collection, no `call` |
| init sample (1 passed, 5 skipped) | 251.72s | 32.76s |
| tensor schema sample (1 passed, 3 skipped) | 52.59s | 25.25s |
| pre-commit | - | all hooks passed |

The init "before" total includes a one-off 152 s memory-settle wait after one case; the per-case `call` times are the like-for-like comparison. Skip reasons in `-rs` match main ("Model is not available online", "`transformers==…` installed, but `transformers<=4.48` is required…"). This PR was also run together with #65441: both modules passed.

CI coverage: the changed modules run in Basic Models (Initialization), Basic Models (Extra Initialization) and Multimodal Processor on NVIDIA and their AMD mirrors, and in the Intel XPU jobs (which select or deselect cases by ID; IDs are unchanged). No model output changes, so no model evaluation applies.

## Details

- `skip_unavailable_models(ids, get_info)` in `tests/models/utils.py` returns the parametrize values, as `pytest.param(..., marks=pytest.mark.skip(reason))` for models that are not available online or fail the transformers version check (`check_max_version=False`, `check_version_reason="vllm"`, the arguments both tests already used). Both test modules use it in their `parametrize` lists, and the same checks are removed from the test bodies.
- The checks only read static fields of the test example registry, so evaluating them at import is cheap and safe. Skips that need the model class or the GPU (`does not support tensor schema validation`, device-capability checks) stay in the test.
- On NVIDIA these cases fork instead of spawning, so the saving there is smaller.
- Independent of #65441; the two touch different hunks and merge cleanly in either order.
- Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for "check_available_online", "test_initialization spawn" and "tensor schema"; none changes where these skips run.
- AI assistance: this change and this description were prepared with an AI coding assistant (Cursor). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix flaky streaming checks in test_translation_validation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the two flaky streaming checks in `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py` that fail now and then in `(MI355 DPX) Entrypoints Integration (Speech to Text)`. The streaming requests get an explicit 30 s timeout, and `test_streaming_response` aligns the words before counting matches instead of comparing them by position.

## Claims

- Fixes `httpx.ReadTimeout` in `test_streaming_response` and `test_stream_options`. Both used httpx's default 5 s timeout. The transcription streaming tests already use 30 s since #20913.
- Fixes `test_streaming_response` failing when one word is dropped or inserted. The 87% threshold is unchanged.
- The check also gets stricter. The old check only looked at as many words as the stream had, so an empty or truncated stream passed. It now fails.

## Validation

CI failures on MI355 DPX. All passed on retry except build 99892, where the first attempt hit the timeout and the retry hit the word check.

- ReadTimeout https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98508#01a18a4b-632f-4951-a936-46dc1ae1302f (`test_stream_options[google/gemma-3n-E2B-it]`)
- ReadTimeout https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100175#01a1aa87-b089-4f16-b28b-1425881adfbe (`test_stream_options[google/gemma-3n-E2B-it]`)
- ReadTimeout https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99892#01a1a5c7-a1cc-4cbc-9538-e19da2d0948f (`test_streaming_response[openai/whisper-small]`)
- Word check https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99609#01a1a25c-88e1-47ef-8688-a788a7fd32ab (`assert 58 >= (76 * 0.87)`)
- Word check https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99743#01a1a3d9-8dcd-491d-8688-577d1e3b1eb4 (`assert 58 >= (76 * 0.87)`)
- Word check https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99892#01a1a5de-506c-4002-a548-f77d48ab9978 (`assert 57 >= (78 * 0.87)`)

The H200 version of the job had no retries over the same period.

**Timeout.** On MI350X the largest gap between two stream chunks of `test_streaming_response[openai/whisper-small]` was 0.065 s. With the client timeout set below that gap, the test fails with the same `httpcore.ReadTimeout` and `httpx.ReadTimeout` chain as in CI. In CI the server had already answered and the stream stalled for more than 5 s in the middle. 30 s keeps a stuck server failing the test.

**Word check.** Both checks run on the real 77 word whisper translation of `foscolo`, with the same cases as in CI and a few broken streams.

| Stream | Old check (`zip`) | New check (`SequenceMatcher` ratio) |
|---|---|---|
| Same text | PASS | 1.000 PASS |
| One word dropped (the CI case) | FAIL | 0.993 PASS |
| One word inserted | FAIL | 0.994 PASS |
| Empty stream | PASS | 0.000 FAIL |
| First half only | PASS | 0.661 FAIL |
| Unrelated text | FAIL | 0.089 FAIL |

**After the fix.** 20 of 20 runs passed on MI350X (CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1a5c0-f715-44fa-97bf-62c86bea67ab`).

```bash
pytest -v entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py -k whisper
```

`google/gemma-3n-E2B-it` is gated and I could not run it locally, so it is covered by the CI jobs of this PR.

## Details

The comment in `test_streaming_response` already says a few tokens may differ between the streaming and the non streaming request. On MI355 DPX that sometimes means one word fewer or one word more around the same spot. Comparing by position then shifts every later word, so a single word difference drops the score from about 99% to 76%. Aligning the two word lists first counts only the words that really differ. `SequenceMatcher.ratio()` is symmetric, which fits two outputs of the same model better than WER against a reference, and it keeps the 87% meaning of the existing threshold. On failure the assert now prints both texts.

Not covered here are two other rare failures in the same job, a `test_wer_correctness` outlier for `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` and GPU memory not released in time between servers.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Cache a PR's ROCm base image for main with `/ci rocm cache`
commits.pr_body:
- `pre-commit.yml`: a PR into main that changes `Dockerfile.rocm_base` or `therock_wheels.py` fails `pre-commit` until a maintainer comments `/ci rocm cache` or `/ci rocm nocache`
- `run_ci_command.py`: `/ci rocm cache` (write access only) starts a main build of AMD CI that copies the stack images the PR's CI built into `rocm/vllm-ci`, by the digests that CI recorded; `/ci rocm nocache` records the choice to skip. Re-running `pre-commit` after either reply clears it
- `build.sh`: a `promote` mode replaces `prebuild`: it copies the recorded stack pair under the key main's `keys_at` gives the PR commit, if the PR uses main's `build.sh` and bake file
- `test_run_ci_command.py`, `test_rocm_build.py`, contributing docs

When a PR changes the ROCm stack, main cold-builds it after merge: main's `Ensure ROCm stack + runtime` took 2 h 42 min after the AITER bump in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63774 (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98819), and the stack inputs changed 24 times in the last 90 days. Since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61939, main does not reuse images from `rocm/vllm-dev`, because PR CI can write any tag there. With this, a maintainer vouches for one PR's images with a comment: they are copied by digest, so overwriting a tag later changes nothing, and main reuses them from its first build after the merge. The `pre-commit` check is a reminder rather than a security boundary and is not tied to a commit: if the PR changes the stack again after caching, main simply builds cold, as today. https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/886 must merge first; `test_run_ci_command.py` (67) and `test_rocm_build.py` (43) pass.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][MooncakeStore] Add automatic deployment cache prefixes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add opt-in `cache_prefix="auto"` to MooncakeStoreConnector so image/model/configuration changes can select a new shared KV namespace without manually calculating a prefix.

## Claims

- Derive a SHA-256 prefix from image identity (falling back to build commit), existing model/cache configuration hashes, and the resolved HF commit.
- Preserve the empty default and literal custom prefixes; scheduler capacities do not affect the automatic prefix.
- Keep the implementation in the Store worker, reusing maintained configuration hashes. The net diff against main is 3 files, +156/−6.

## Validation

- 9 focused CPU tests passed on the merged branch: `python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_cache_prefix.py -q` in a uv-managed Python 3.12 environment.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed against upstream main, including Ruff, mypy, markdown lint and test tethering.
- Real GPU startup and Mooncake transfers have not been validated locally. This remains a draft starting point; no accuracy or performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Updated to incorporate Nicolò Lucchesi's simplification from https://github.com/hj-mistral/vllm/pull/3. This removes the parallel config exclusion lists, environment scan, quantization object serializer and dedicated GPU CI step from the original version. Existing CPU CI collects the focused tests.

Automatic mode requires an immutable image identity or known build commit and an immutable model identity. Environment flags and live/overwritten weight files are outside this first pass; use a custom prefix when they change without a corresponding identity change. The image tag takes precedence over the commit.

This namespace is not a complete payload-compatibility validator: deployments sharing it must still use compatible Store layouts and parallel topologies. In particular, rank numbers alone do not distinguish TP/PP sizes in the default rank-local layout. The resolved payload fingerprint proposed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56971 is complementary work.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Use file:// rendezvous in the Ray multi-GPU test harness
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a flaky `EADDRINUSE` in `(MI300) Distributed Features`: [AMD CI #13691](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13691/list?sid=01a0e73f-5f85-4e70-8fb6-fc77bd1d7c40&tab=output)

```
FAILED tests/distributed/test_quick_all_reduce.py::test_custom_quick_allreduce[test_target1-1-2-INT8]
  torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to listen on any local network
  address. port: 34645, useIpv6: false, code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE, message: address already in use
```

`init_test_distributed_environment` builds a TCP rendezvous from a port `multi_process_parallel` took from `get_open_port()`, which closes its probe socket before returning the number. Rank 0 binds that port ~1s later inside a Ray worker (measured 0.98-1.11s) and nothing holds it in between. Every vended port lands in the ephemeral range `32768-60999`, which contains the 34645 above, and the helper has no cross-process coordination: the same port went to two processes 3 times in 480 vends. AMD CI containers run with `--network host`, so concurrent jobs share one range.

This is the probe-then-bind pattern #50999 removed from the single-node executors. RFC #51275 lists the test call sites as Category I, deliberately deferred to "a dedicated test-infrastructure change" using "a test-owned listener or file rendezvous". This is that change for the Ray multi-GPU harness; #58312, #56595, #53221 and #52366 do the same for other harnesses.

**Change** 
Use a `FileStore` rendezvous as the executors do, so there is no port to bind. The path comes from the token the ranks already share, because `init_test_distributed_environment` runs in every Ray worker and the `uuid4()` in `get_file_store_init_method()` would give each rank a different path. `multi_process_parallel` removes the file afterwards. ROCm + AITER custom all-reduce keeps TCP through the existing `aiter_requires_tcp_store()` gate, since its IPC metadata exchange asserts on `TCPStore`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/distributed/test_quick_all_reduce.py::test_custom_quick_allreduce -k test_target1
pytest -q tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
```

At a sub-1% rate the race is not reachable by repetition, so it was checked as in #50999: occupy the vended port before the rendezvous binds it.

## Test Result

MI300X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.13, 2 GPUs.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `test_custom_quick_allreduce -k test_target1`, incl. the `INT8` case that failed in CI | 5 passed, 5 skipped |
| `test_custom_all_reduce.py` | 48 passed, 3 skipped |
| squatter on the vended port, before the change | `DistNetworkError ... code: -98, EADDRINUSE` |
| rendezvous files left in `/tmp` | 0 |
